description: Desktop publishing (DTP) uses computer software to combine text and graphics into well-designed publications such as newsletters, brochures, flyers and posters.

mcq.questionText: What does the term 'desktop publishing' (DTP) mean?

options.text: Using a computer to create page layouts that combine text and graphics for printing or publishing
Storing files on a computer desktop folder
Sending documents over the internet to a printer

mcq.explanation: DTP is the use of specialised software on a personal computer to design and arrange text and images into a finished publication ready for printing or sharing.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of desktop publishing software?
mcq.explanation: Microsoft Publisher is a popular DTP program. Other examples include Adobe InDesign, Adobe PageMaker and Scribus.

mcq.questionText: Which publication is most likely produced using desktop publishing software?

options.text: A school newsletter with columns and photographs

mcq.explanation: Newsletters, brochures, flyers and posters that mix text and graphics in a designed layout are typical DTP products.

mcq.questionText: What is the main difference between word processing and desktop publishing?

options.text: Word processing cannot type any text
DTP focuses on precise page layout and design, while word processing focuses on creating and editing text
Word processing can only be used on the internet

mcq.explanation: Word processors are designed mainly for writing and editing text, while DTP programs give greater control over arranging text and graphics on the page.

mcq.questionText: In a DTP program, what is a text frame (text box) used for?

options.text: To hold and position blocks of text on the page
To save the publication to disk
To connect the computer to a printer

mcq.explanation: A text frame is a container that holds text and can be moved or resized so the designer controls exactly where the text sits on the page.

mcq.questionText: What is the purpose of a master page in a DTP publication?

options.text: To lock the document so it cannot be edited
To hold elements such as headers, footers and page numbers that repeat on many pages
To store only the first page of a document

mcq.explanation: A master page contains repeating items that appear automatically on every page based on it, ensuring consistency across the publication.

mcq.questionText: Which feature lets text flow neatly around a picture in a publication?
mcq.explanation: Text wrapping arranges text so that it runs around the edges of an image instead of overlapping it.

mcq.questionText: What is a template in desktop publishing?

options.text: A ready-made design that can be reused as a starting point for a publication
A printer setting for paper size

mcq.explanation: Templates provide a pre-designed layout, saving time and helping users create professional publications quickly.

mcq.questionText: Which design principle is about using clearly different sizes, colours or styles to make important items stand out?
mcq.explanation: Contrast uses noticeable differences, such as bold or large headings against small body text, to draw the reader's attention.

mcq.questionText: What does the design principle of 'alignment' refer to in a publication?

options.text: Lining up text and objects neatly along common edges or lines
Adding many different fonts on one page

mcq.explanation: Alignment arranges elements so their edges line up, giving the page a tidy and organised appearance.

mcq.questionText: Why are guides and rulers useful in DTP software?

options.text: They help position and align objects accurately on the page
They automatically write the text for the user
They connect the publication to the internet

mcq.explanation: Rulers show measurements and guides are reference lines, both helping the designer place and align items precisely.

mcq.questionText: What does 'grouping' objects in a DTP program allow you to do?

options.text: Treat several objects as one so they can be moved or resized together
Change the language of the text

mcq.explanation: Grouping combines multiple objects into one unit so they can be handled together without losing their relative positions.

mcq.questionText: What is the role of 'white space' in publication design?

options.text: It wastes paper and should always be removed
It is empty space that makes a layout less crowded and easier to read
It is a special font colour
It is the space used to store the file

mcq.explanation: White space is the unused area around and between elements; it improves readability and gives a clean, balanced look.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a typical step when producing a publication in DTP?

options.text: Planning the layout, then adding and arranging text and graphics

mcq.explanation: Producing a publication involves planning the design, setting up the page, adding text and graphics, arranging them, then proofreading and printing.

mcq.questionText: What is the purpose of using columns in a publication such as a newsletter?

options.text: To divide text into vertical sections that are easier to read
To stop the document from printing

mcq.explanation: Columns split text into narrow vertical blocks, which improves readability and gives newsletters and magazines a professional look.

fib.questionText: The short form _____ stands for desktop publishing.
fib.explanation: DTP is the common abbreviation for desktop publishing.

fib.questionText: A _____ is a container used to hold and position text on a page in DTP software.
fib.explanation: A text frame, also called a text box, holds blocks of text and can be moved or resized.

fib.questionText: A _____ page contains repeating items such as page numbers and headers that appear on many pages.
fib.explanation: Master pages store elements that should appear consistently across the publication.

fib.questionText: A ready-made design used as a starting point for a publication is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Templates provide a pre-built layout that saves time and ensures a professional result.

fib.questionText: The feature that makes text flow around the edges of a picture is called text _____.
fib.explanation: Text wrapping arranges text so it surrounds an image neatly.

fib.questionText: The empty area left around and between objects to avoid a crowded look is called _____ space.
fib.explanation: White space improves readability and gives a clean, balanced design.

fib.questionText: An open-source DTP program that is free to use is called _____.
fib.explanation: Scribus is a free, open-source desktop publishing program.

fib.questionText: Lining up text and objects neatly along common edges is the design principle of _____.
fib.explanation: Alignment gives a publication a tidy and organised appearance.

fib.questionText: Combining several objects so they can be moved or resized as one unit is called _____.
fib.explanation: Grouping keeps objects together while preserving their positions.

fib.questionText: Dividing the text of a newsletter into vertical sections is done by using _____.
fib.explanation: Columns make long text easier to read and give a professional layout.

tf.questionText: Desktop publishing software is mainly used to design page layouts that combine text and graphics.
tf.explanation: DTP focuses on arranging text and images into well-designed publications.

tf.questionText: Microsoft Publisher is an example of desktop publishing software.
tf.explanation: Microsoft Publisher is one of the most widely used DTP programs.

tf.questionText: Word processing and desktop publishing are exactly the same and have no differences.
tf.explanation: Word processing focuses on creating and editing text, while DTP focuses on precise page layout and design.

tf.questionText: A master page is used to store items that repeat on many pages of a publication.
tf.explanation: Master pages hold repeating elements such as headers, footers and page numbers.

tf.questionText: Templates make it slower and harder to create publications.
tf.explanation: Templates speed up the work by providing ready-made designs to start from.

tf.questionText: Text wrapping allows text to flow around an image instead of overlapping it.
tf.explanation: Text wrapping arranges text neatly around the edges of a picture.

tf.questionText: White space should always be completely removed from a publication.
tf.explanation: White space is helpful; it reduces crowding and improves readability.

tf.questionText: Brochures, flyers, business cards and posters can all be produced using DTP software.
tf.explanation: These are common publications created with desktop publishing programs.

tf.questionText: Guides and rulers in DTP software help to position and align objects accurately.
tf.explanation: Rulers show measurements and guides act as reference lines for accurate placement.

tf.questionText: Using too many different fonts on one page is a good design practice that improves consistency.
tf.explanation: Good design keeps fonts limited and consistent; too many fonts make a publication look untidy.

summary.correctAnswer: DTP is the use of computer software to design and arrange text and graphics into finished publications for printing or sharing.
summary.explanation: This captures the core idea that DTP combines text and images into designed layouts.

summary.questionText: State the main difference between word processing and desktop publishing.
summary.correctAnswer: Word processing focuses on creating and editing text, while DTP focuses on precise page layout and design of text and graphics.
summary.explanation: Each tool has a different main purpose even though both can handle text and images.

summary.questionText: Give three examples of desktop publishing software.
summary.correctAnswer: Microsoft Publisher, Adobe InDesign (or PageMaker), and Scribus.
summary.explanation: These are common DTP programs used to create publications.

summary.questionText: List four types of publications that can be produced using DTP.
summary.correctAnswer: Newsletters, brochures, flyers, and posters (also business cards, magazines, certificates and calendars).
summary.explanation: DTP is used to produce a wide range of designed printed materials.

summary.questionText: What is a text frame and why is it useful?
summary.correctAnswer: A text frame is a container that holds text; it lets the designer position and resize text exactly where it is needed on the page.
summary.explanation: Text frames give control over where text appears in the layout.

summary.questionText: Explain the purpose of a master page.
summary.correctAnswer: A master page holds elements such as headers, footers and page numbers that repeat automatically on many pages, keeping the publication consistent.
summary.explanation: Master pages save time and ensure a uniform look across pages.

summary.questionText: Name four basic design principles used in publications.
summary.correctAnswer: Alignment, contrast, balance, and consistency (plus careful use of fonts, colour and white space).
summary.explanation: These principles guide the creation of clear and attractive publications.

summary.questionText: What is the benefit of using templates in DTP?
summary.correctAnswer: Templates provide ready-made designs that save time and help users produce professional publications quickly.
summary.explanation: Templates remove the need to design every layout from scratch.

summary.questionText: Outline the main steps in producing a publication using DTP.
summary.correctAnswer: Plan the design, set up the page and layout, add and arrange text and graphics, apply formatting, proofread, then print or publish.
summary.explanation: Following ordered steps produces a neat, error-free publication.

summary.questionText: State two reasons why desktop publishing is important.
summary.correctAnswer: It allows people to create professional-looking publications cheaply and quickly, and it gives full control over the design and layout of materials.
summary.explanation: DTP makes professional design accessible to schools, businesses and individuals.

hoq.questionText: A school wants to create a two-page newsletter where the same school logo, name and page number must appear automatically on both pages without retyping them. Which DTP feature should be used?
hoq.explanation: Placing the logo, name and page number on a master page makes them appear automatically on every page based on it, avoiding repetition and keeping the design consistent.

hoq.questionText: A student designs a flyer using six different fonts, bright clashing colours and objects scattered with no straight edges. Which design principles has the student most clearly failed to apply?
hoq.explanation: Using too many fonts and clashing colours breaks consistency, and scattering objects without lining them up breaks alignment, so the flyer looks untidy and unprofessional.

hoq.questionText: A designer wants a photograph and its caption to always move together as one item whenever the photo is repositioned in a brochure. What should the designer do?

options.text: Group the photograph and the caption text together
Apply text wrapping to the caption
Save the brochure as a template
Add more columns to the page

hoq.explanation: Grouping combines the photo and caption into a single unit so they move and resize together, keeping the caption attached to its image.
